thread:
Maya R.: Hey team — PR #12841 is blocked in the merge queue. Failing intermittently on `integration/shard-4` and CI keeps rerunning but it's inconsistent. Need a quick plan: approval to force-merge, snapshot update, or debug the flake? :thinking:

Liam T.: Can you paste the failing log? if it's a snapshot mismatch we can update, but if it's nondeterministic we should rerun a couple times then consider flaky mark.

Maya R.: Pasting the last failing excerpt: ```
FAIL tests/integration/test_streaming.py::test_stream_chunked_processing[shard-4] 
AssertionError: expected 3 chunks, got 1
  at /workspace/redwood/runtime/streamer.py:214
Logs show timeout on the second chunk, then process exits.
```

Alex P.: Looks like a timing flake — often happens when the test runs on shard-4 with low headroom. Could be a transient GPU scheduler delay.

CI Bot: Rerun requested by Maya R. — CI job 12841.2 queued (shard-4). <https://ci.redwood.example/12841/2|view job>

DevOps Bot: Merge queue hold enabled for PR #12841 due to failing checks. Current position: 3.

Karen W.: @Sam H. do you have bandwidth to give an approval if we decide to force? I want to avoid hiding a real regression.

Sam H.: I can approve if we confirm it's flaky and we add a flaky-ticket/label. Do we have repro locally?

Maya R.: Not reliably — I tried `pytest tests/integration/test_streaming.py::test_stream_chunked_processing -k shard4 -x` locally; it passed 2/3 times. I can run a 10x loop and collect traces.

Liam T.: Before force-merge, try: 1) rebase onto main (we had a scheduling fix merged) 2) trigger CI rerun 3) if still flaky, add `@flaky` with issue link and request approval. If rebase reduces failures, we can re-run and merge.

Maya R.: Rebased and pushed. Triggering rerun now.

CI Bot: Rerun triggered by Maya R. — CI job 12841.3 started (shard-4).

Alex P.: If the rerun fails again, paste full `pytest -k shard4 -vv` with `--durations=20` output. Also consider changing the test to be less timing-sensitive (use `wait_for_condition()` instead of fixed sleep).

CI Bot: CI job 12841.3 failed on shard-4 — same assertion. (logs: https://ci.redwood.example/12841/3)

Maya R.: OK failing again. I'll open a mini-issue to track flake and add the label. Will we be allowed to force-merge for hotfix?

Karen W.: Add the `flake:intermittent` label and link the ticket. I'll +1 approval once that's in place and we add a short note in PR description. We prefer not to hide regressions, but this is blocking a critical rollout.

Maya R.: Done: https://tickets.redwood.example/INC-4823 — added description, repro attempts, and logs. PR updated with the ticket link and label.

Sam H.: Reviewed the PR changes (small scheduling tweak). Given the triage, I'm OK to approve and let the rollback path exist if we see issues in canary. Approving now.

CI Bot: Approval added by Sam H.

DevOps Bot: Merge queue hold released for PR #12841. PR is eligible to merge when it reaches head-of-queue.

Maya R.: Thanks all. I'll monitor canary rollout and open a follow-up PR to make the test deterministic (switch to event-based wait).

Alex P.: Thanks — can you cc me on the follow-up? I can help refactor the test. :thumbsup:

Maya R.: Will do. Closing the loop: PR merged and canary started. CI job 12841.4 (post-merge smoke) passed.

CI Bot: CI job 12841.4 passed. Canary rollout at 10% started.

Karen W.: Nice — good triage. Please file the test-fix within 3 business days.

Maya R.: Filed: https://tickets.redwood.example/ENG-2127 -- assigning to Alex P.

Alex P.: Acknowledged, will pick it up tomorrow.

Maya R.: Thanks everyone :party:
